messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Cross-region routing anomaly detected — elevated 5xx rates and steering churn between eu-west2 <-> us-west1. Aggregate 5xx up ~9% over baseline. Top symptom: large fraction of short-lived pins and rebalances. Monitoring: https://internal.monitor/redwood/alerts/4400123456 :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): I'm on it. Pulling up graphs and routing logs. Is this customer-facing or internal probe noise?

sanjay (eng-runtime): Looks customer-facing — I see user traffic errors correlating with steering flips. Querying route controller logs now. Policy delta shows a canary policy rollout (route-policy v1.13) at 03:45 UTC that modified tie-break weighting for region affinity.

eli (eng-sre): Can we confirm which prefixes/regions are affected? CS is getting tickets from multiple EU customers. @alex (support) can you drop any top customer IDs?

alex (support): Yep — three customers in EU reporting 502/timeout spikes since ~03:46. I'll open a ticket summary for each and paste here.

tara (network): I pulled the control-plane diff. The new comparator introduced a fractional weight fallback that, under certain latency tie conditions, doesn't stabilize — it produces micro-oscillation between eu-west2 and us-west1. Basically a rounding/float compare bug causing partial route bleed.

maria (oncall): That sounds like a policy misroute. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Roll back route-policy v1.13 to v1.12 (fast). 2) Apply an emergency static pin for impacted prefixes. Which is lower-risk and faster?

sanjay (eng-runtime): Rollback is straightforward and should stop the churn. I'll trigger a rollback to v1.12 for the policy scope affecting /model-api/* and /embed-api/*. Command I will run:

```bash
# rollback to previous stable policy version
redwoodctl routing policy rollback --name cross-region-affinity --to-version v1.12 --scope "/model-api/*,/embed-api/*" --force --reason "emergency rollback: fractional-weight bleed"
```

eli (eng-sre): If you can kick that, I'll watch the metrics and the KV cache behavior. Also temporarily disable automatic steer during rollback to avoid flip-flopping.

deploy-bot: route-policy rollback initiated by sanjay. Change ID cp-4400123456-RB. Estimated propagation: 30-60s per region.

maria (oncall): Notifying status page and PS teams. Alex, paste a short customer-facing blurb we can use.

alex (support): Draft for status: "We are investigating degraded request success rates in EU regions affecting short requests; mitigation in progress. We will provide updates every 15 minutes."

eli (eng-sre): Observability update: pre-rollback 5xx=9%, lat p95 eu-west2 rose 220ms. Starting at rollback start timestamp.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Rollback command completed. Controller accepted v1.12 as active. Pushing disable-steer flag for the affected scope now:

```bash
redwoodctl routing set --scope "/model-api/*,/embed-api/*" --steer-enabled false --reason "stabilize during rollback"
```

deploy-bot: steer-disabled for scope /model-api/*,/embed-api/* by sanjay. Change ID cp-4400123456-DISABLE.

eli (eng-sre): Seeing immediate reduction in policy churn in the controller logs. 5xx trending down. Hold for 5m and confirm customer ticket correlation.

maria (oncall): Assigning followup tasks: postmortem owner = eli, mitigation verification = sanjay, customer comms = alex, root-cause network analysis = tara. ETA initial RCA notes in 48h.

alex (support): Update posted to status.redwood: "Mitigation: routing policy rollback and steering temporarily disabled for affected API endpoints. Customers may see intermittent improvement as caches converge. We will update in 15 minutes."

eli (eng-sre): After 6m: 5xx down to baseline (~0.8%), p95 latency back to normal. Customer reports are decreasing. Recommend to keep steer disabled until we validate a patched comparator.

tara (network): I reproduced locally — comparator treats tie when abs(delta) < 1e-6 as equal, but subsequent weight normalization introduced a tiny non-determinism causing oscillation. Patch ready: change tie logic to deterministic stable ordering based on region priority, add unit tests.

maria (oncall): Good. For immediate completeness: leave steer disabled, don't reintroduce v1.13. sanjay please coordinate a canary of patched comparator in a single non-prod region then promote.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Will do. Pushing a canary job to staging eu-west2 in ~45m. Also adding e2e test covering tie-break scenario to prevent regression.

eli (eng-sre): I'll close the pager once we confirm 30m of stable metrics and no new customer tickets. Current plan: monitor for 30m then declare recovery.

maria (oncall): Not closing yet — but thanks everyone. Small post-incident notes: immediate impact was customer-facing errors for select endpoints due to policy-induced routing flapping. Mitigation: rollback + disable steer. Next steps: patch comparator, add deterministic ordering, add regression tests, improve rollout canary gating for routing policy changes.

deploy-bot: Change cp-4400123456-RB marked success. cp-4400123456-DISABLE applied across regions.

eli (eng-sre): 30m check-in: metrics stable, no new tickets. I'm marking this as mitigated — will prepare RCA and timeline.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. Closing incident thread and creating postmortem doc: /docs/incidents/4400123456-routing-signal-shadow-postmortem.md.

alex (support): I'll follow up with customers with a summary and apology.

tara (network): I'll open PR for patch and request expedited review.

sanjay (eng-runtime): Filed a bug: RB-4400123456 "floating-weight comparator nondeterministic tie leads to routing oscillation". Priorities: high.

maria (oncall): Closing communications loop. If anything reappears ping #oncall immediately. :white_check_mark:
